definitions.gloss: touting; soliciting customers on the street
definitions.explanation: The act of approaching people on the street to invite them into a shop, restaurant, or establishment.
A person who stands outside a business and tries to attract customers by calling out to passersby. Common in entertainment districts.

notes:
USAGE:
{客引|きゃくひ}き combines ⟦{客|きゃく}→客：00865_kyaku⟧ (customer) and {引|ひ}き (pulling). It can refer to either the act of soliciting or the person doing it. {客引|きゃくひ}き⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧ means to tout or solicit. In many Japanese cities, aggressive touting is regulated or banned by local ordinances.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {客引|きゃくひ}き⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧ (to tout, to solicit customers)
- {客引|きゃくひ}き⟦{禁止|きんし}→禁止：02643_kinshi⟧ (touting prohibited)
- {客引|きゃくひ}き⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{声|こえ}→声：02207_koe⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦かけられる→かける：00854_kakeru⟧ (to be approached by a tout)
- ⟦しつこい→しつこい：06498_shitsukoi⟧{客引|きゃくひ}き (persistent touting)

SIMILAR WORDS:
⟦{呼|よ}び{込|こ}み→呼び込む：06087_yobikomu⟧ refers to barkers calling out to attract customers, often at markets or street stalls. {客引|きゃくひ}き has a more negative connotation and is associated with nightlife districts.
